people.name: Alice
people.tagline: A curious little girl who falls down a rabbit hole into a world of nonsense.
people.appearance: A little girl; referred to as 'the poor little thing' after shrinking. Grows to more than nine feet high, then shrinks to about two feet high; wears one of the Rabbit's little white kid gloves. Tiny little thing before drinking; grows to fill the room with head pressing ceiling, elbow against door, arm out window, foot up chimney; shrinks back to about normal. Three inches high during the conversation; later possesses an immense length of neck like a stalk; finally nine inches high.
people.personality: Curious, impulsive, talkative, eager, polite, and prone to tears. She is fond of giving herself advice she seldom follows and constantly tries to apply her school lessons to make sense of things. Her flaw is speaking quickly without thinking of consequences, leading to misunderstandings. She holds dear her sense of order and manners.
people.background: A little girl from the surface world who falls down a rabbit hole. She can change size by eating and drinking various items, and attempts to use rote-learned school lessons to navigate Wonderland.

relationships.name: White Rabbit
relationships.note: Follows him underground; he mistakes her for his housemaid Mary Ann.

relationships.name: Dinah
relationships.note: Worries about her cat and accidentally offends others by praising her.

relationships.name: Mouse
relationships.note: Offends the Mouse by talking about Dinah.

relationships.name: Duchess
relationships.note: Interacts with her in the kitchen and later at croquet.

relationships.name: Gryphon
relationships.note: Escorted by him to the Mock Turtle.

relationships.name: Alice's sister
relationships.note: Sits with her on the bank before falling asleep.

people.name: White Rabbit
people.tagline: A perpetually late, waistcoat-wearing rabbit whose panic draws Alice underground.
people.appearance: White fur, pink eyes, wears a waistcoat with a pocket, carries a watch. Splendidly dressed, carrying a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other. Has paws, fur, and whiskers. Later seen with a trumpet in one hand and a scroll of parchment in the other.
people.personality: Perpetually anxious, hurried, muttering to himself, and easily startled. He is bossy, quick to anger, and orders everyone about—even threatening to burn his own house down—yet remains terrified of the Duchess and the Queen. He smiles nervously at everything when afraid. His flaw is his overwhelming, paralyzing fear of authority.
people.background: A talking rabbit who serves as a herald or attendant in Wonderland. He can organize other animals and commands some authority over them, but lives in constant dread of his superiors.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Draws her underground; mistakes her for his housemaid Mary Ann.

relationships.name: Duchess
relationships.note: Terrified of keeping her waiting and facing her savagery.

people.name: Queen of Hearts
people.tagline: The tyrannical ruler of the card court who constantly orders beheadings to settle any difficulty.
people.personality: Tyrannical, impatient, and prone to screaming execution orders for every slight. She holds dear her absolute authority and her flaw is her uncontrollable rage.
people.background: Ruler of Wonderland's card court who oversees croquet games and trials, settling all difficulties by ordering beheadings.

relationships.name: King of Hearts
relationships.note: He timidly intervenes but ultimately defers to her fury.

relationships.name: Knave of Hearts
relationships.note: She presides over his trial for stealing tarts.

relationships.name: Bill the Lizard
relationships.note: She strikes him with her inkstand during the trial.

people.name: Duchess
people.tagline: An ugly, violent noblewoman who nurses a baby in a smoky kitchen and moralizes about everything.
people.appearance: Very ugly, exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, uncomfortably sharp chin.
people.personality: Initially violent, rude, and prone to shouting sudden insults or orders. Later becomes overly affectionate, moralizing, and eager to agree with everything Alice says. Her flaw is her extreme volatility and physical aggression.
people.background: A noblewoman in Wonderland who lives in a smoke-filled kitchen with a cook and a baby. She is invited to play croquet with the Queen and is briefly sentenced to execution.

relationships.name: White Rabbit
relationships.note: He fears her savagery if he keeps her waiting.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Throws her baby at Alice; later rests her sharp chin on Alice's shoulder.

people.name: King of Hearts
people.tagline: The timid king who occasionally tempers the Queen's fury but defers to her authority.
people.appearance: Wears a great wig with his crown over it, wears spectacles.
people.personality: Timid before the Queen but decisive in wanting annoyances gone; authoritarian yet ineffectual, quick to threaten execution but easily flustered. He holds dear order but his flaw is his cowardice.
people.background: Co-ruler of the card court who runs wildly about looking for order and presides as judge over the Knave's trial.

relationships.name: Queen of Hearts
relationships.note: He fears her and begs her to calm down or remove things she dislikes.

relationships.name: Knave of Hearts
relationships.note: Presides over his trial as judge.

people.name: Gryphon
people.tagline: A bossy, chuckling creature who escorts Alice and dismisses the Queen's authority.
people.age: of unknown age, a mythical creature (an adult)
people.personality: Chuckling, dismissive of authority, impatient with questions, bossy, and physically forceful. He shakes and punches the Mock Turtle and drags Alice by the hand, yet acts as a helpful informant whispering explanations to her. His flaw is his rough impatience.
people.background: A mythical creature ordered by the Queen to escort Alice. He knows the inner workings of Wonderland's justice system and reveals that the Queen's executions are merely fancy.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Ordered to take her to the Mock Turtle; drags her to the trial and whispers court customs to her.

people.name: Caterpillar
people.tagline: A languid, hookah-smoking creature who questions identity.
people.age: of unknown age (a larval stage of life)
people.appearance: Large, blue, exactly three inches high, sitting with arms folded (which later unfold), smoking a long hookah atop a mushroom.
people.personality: Utterly composed, indifferent, languid, sleepy, stern, contemptuous, and easily offended about its height. It holds dear its own composure and wisdom, but its flaw is its condescension toward others.
people.background: A three-inch-high creature living atop a large mushroom in Wonderland. It possesses knowledge of the mushroom's magical properties and tests others' memories with poetry.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Questions her identity, tests her memory, and teaches her how to use the mushroom.

people.name: Cheshire Cat
people.tagline: A grinning cat that vanishes at will, leaving only its smile.
people.appearance: A large cat grinning from ear to ear, with very long claws and a great many teeth. Appears gradually starting with just a grin, then eyes, ears, and finally the whole head.
people.personality: Calm, philosophical, impertinent, and unbothered by the chaos around it. It holds dear its own amusement and detachment, with its flaw being its complete lack of urgency or empathy for others' distress.
people.background: Belongs to the Duchess. Capable of appearing and vanishing at will, sometimes leaving only its grin behind. Lives in the wood near the Hatter and March Hare.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Gives her directions and explains that everyone is mad.

relationships.name: Duchess
relationships.note: Belongs to the Duchess.

relationships.name: Hatter
relationships.note: Suggests Alice visit him.

relationships.name: March Hare
relationships.note: Suggests Alice visit him.

people.name: Hatter
people.tagline: A rude, mad tea-party guest who quarrelled with Time.
people.age: adult (a grown man, a tradesman by his hat and station)
people.appearance: Carries a watch that tells the day of the month but not the hour; uses a teaspoon; carries a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other; wears shoes that shake off; wears a hat that isn't his.
people.personality: Contemptuous, mournful about his past, exceedingly rude, trembling, and terrified of the Queen. He holds dear his tea-time rituals, but his flaw is his rudeness and inability to answer his own riddles.
people.background: A mad person living in one direction from the wood. He had a quarrel with Time, resulting in it always being six o'clock. Called as the first witness at the trial.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Exceedingly rude to her at the tea-party.

relationships.name: March Hare
relationships.note: Shares the perpetual tea-party and appears in court.

relationships.name: Dormouse
relationships.note: Uses him as a cushion at the tea-party.

relationships.name: Time
relationships.note: Quarrelled with Time, causing the eternal tea-time.

relationships.name: Queen of Hearts
relationships.note: Terrified of her during the trial.

people.name: March Hare
people.tagline: The mad host of the perpetual tea-party.
people.age: an adult (a mad creature of Wonderland)
people.appearance: Seen arm-in-arm with the Dormouse at court.
people.personality: Meek when scolded by the Hatter but uncivil, argumentative, contradictory, and hurried toward Alice. He holds dear his hospitality (however flawed), but his flaw is his madness and incivility.
people.background: A mad person living in another direction from the wood. Hosts a perpetual tea-party under a tree in front of his house with the Hatter and the Dormouse.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Uncivil and argumentative toward her.

relationships.name: Hatter
relationships.note: Meek when scolded by him; shares the tea-party and court appearance.

relationships.name: Dormouse
relationships.note: Uses him as a cushion; walks arm-in-arm with him in court.

people.name: Mock Turtle
people.tagline: A sorrowful creature from which Mock Turtle Soup is made, who was once a real Turtle and recounts his sea-school days.
people.appearance: Large eyes full of tears, flappers, stiff body, cheeks that tears run down.
people.personality: Melancholy, pedantic, prone to long silences and heavy sobbing. Perpetually sorrowful, sighing deeply, weeping, and speaking slowly and sadly. He holds dear his memories of being a real turtle, and his flaw is his inability to move past his grief.
people.background: Once a real Turtle who attended school in the sea, now transformed into the ingredient for Mock Turtle Soup.

people.name: Dinah
people.tagline: Alice's beloved pet cat, praised for catching mice but feared by Wonderland's creatures.
people.appearance: Not present in Wonderland; described as a dear quiet thing who sits purring by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face. A nice soft thing, capital one for catching mice.
people.personality: Quiet, soft, and an excellent hunter of mice. She is deeply loved by Alice but inadvertently causes terror among the smaller creatures of Wonderland.
people.background: Alice's pet cat left behind on the surface. She cannot do anything in Wonderland, but her mere mention drives the plot by scattering Alice's new acquaintances.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Alice worries she will miss her at tea-time and praises her hunting skills.

relationships.name: Mouse
relationships.note: The Mouse is terrified of her because she catches mice.

people.name: Bill the Lizard
people.tagline: A helpless juror perpetually victimized by the chaos of the trial.
people.appearance: Poor little thing waving its tail about; mouth open gazing at the roof; ink trickling down his face.
people.personality: Helpless, confused, and perpetually victimized by the chaos around him. He holds dear his attempt to do his duty but his flaw is his complete inability to cope with disruption.
people.background: A lizard serving as a juryman in the trial of the Knave of Hearts.

relationships.name: Queen of Hearts
relationships.note: Struck by her inkstand during the trial.

people.name: Knave of Hearts
people.tagline: The royal attendant accused of stealing the Queen's tarts.
people.appearance: Carries the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion; later stands in chains with a soldier on each side to guard him.
people.personality: Obedient and careful as an attendant, then a passive prisoner awaiting verdict. He holds dear his duty but lacks agency.
people.background: A card servant who carries the crown and is put on trial for stealing the Queen's tarts.

relationships.name: King of Hearts
relationships.note: Carries his crown on a cushion.

relationships.name: Queen of Hearts
relationships.note: Stands trial before her for stealing tarts.

people.name: Alice's sister
people.tagline: Alice’s older sister who wakes her from the dream and imagines Wonderland afterward

people.name: Dodo
people.tagline: A solemn, self-important bird who organizes the Caucus-race.
people.personality: Solemn, officious, and self-important. He holds dear his authority over the group's activities, but his flaw is his pomposity and tendency to use long words no one understands.
people.background: A bird who fell into the pool of tears and swam to shore with Alice and the others. He can organize events and declare outcomes, though he hides no particular secret.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Presents her own thimble back to her as a prize.

relationships.name: Lory
relationships.note: Swam to shore together.

relationships.name: Eaglet
relationships.note: Swam to shore together; gets told by the Eaglet to speak English.

people.name: Mouse
people.tagline: The offended storyteller of the pool of tears who dries the party with a history lesson

people.name: Dormouse
people.tagline: A chronically sleepy creature used as a cushion at the tea-party.
people.personality: Perpetually drowsy, speaks in its sleep, easily irritated when woken, sleepy, sulky, and prone to being shouted at. It holds dear its rest, but its flaw is its inability to stay awake or be taken seriously.
people.background: A participant in the perpetual tea-party, constantly stuffed into the teapot or used as a cushion by the March Hare and the Hatter. Tells stories while half-asleep.

relationships.name: Hatter
relationships.note: Used as a cushion by him; shouted at by him.

relationships.name: March Hare
relationships.note: Used as a cushion by him; walks arm-in-arm with him in court.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Complains about her growing in court.

people.name: Eaglet
people.tagline: A blunt bird amused by others' pomposity.
people.personality: Blunt and amused by others' pomposity. It values plain speaking and finds humor in pretension, lacking any notable hidden flaw beyond its abruptness.
people.background: A bird that fell into the pool of tears and swam to shore with Alice and the others.

relationships.name: Dodo
relationships.note: Tells him to speak English and hides a smile at his pomposity.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Swam to shore together.

relationships.name: Lory
relationships.note: Swam to shore together.

people.name: Lory
people.tagline: A sulky bird who argues about its age.
people.personality: Sulky and defensive about its age. It values seniority and being right, but its flaw is its quickness to take offense and sulk.
people.background: A bird that fell into the pool of tears and swam to shore with Alice and the others.

relationships.name: Alice
relationships.note: Argues with her about who knows better due to age.

relationships.name: Dodo
relationships.note: Swam to shore together.

relationships.name: Eaglet
relationships.note: Swam to shore together.

world.name: little door
world.summary: A fifteen-inch-high door hidden behind a low curtain in the Hall of Doors, unlocked by the golden key.
world.body: The little door is about fifteen inches high, hidden behind a low curtain in the hall.

world.name: rabbit-hole
world.summary: The entrance to Wonderland under the hedge.
world.body: A large hole under a hedge that leads straight like a tunnel before dipping suddenly into a very deep well.

world.name: court of justice
world.summary: The courtroom where the King and Queen of Hearts hold the trial of the Knave.
world.body: The courtroom where the King and Queen of Hearts hold the trial of the Knave, filled with birds, beasts, and the whole pack of cards.

world.name: Croquet-ground
world.summary: The Queen's croquet ground where live animals are used as equipment.
world.body: The ground is ridges and furrows; balls are live hedgehogs, mallets are live flamingoes, and arches are soldiers bending double.

world.name: Hall of Doors
world.summary: The underground hall Alice first lands in, ringed by locked doors and containing the glass table and little door.
world.body: An underground hall lit by a row of lamps hanging from the roof, ringed entirely by locked doors. All doors around the hall are locked except the little door behind the curtain. The great hall with the glass table and the little door has vanished completely since Alice's swim in the pool of tears.

world.name: March Hare's house
world.summary: A very large house belonging to the March Hare, recognizable by its ear-shaped chimneys and fur-thatched roof.
world.body: The March Hare's house has chimneys shaped like ears and a roof thatched with fur.

world.name: pool of tears
world.summary: A pool of salt water created by Alice's crying when she was giant-sized.
world.body: A pool of salt water about four inches deep reaching half down the hall, created by Alice's crying when she was ten feet tall. The pool of tears is made of salt water.

events.what: Created by Alice's crying when she was giant-sized.

world.name: Tree in the wood
world.summary: A tree in the wood with a door leading right into it, which opens directly into the long hall.
world.body: One of the trees in the wood has a door leading right into it, which opens into the long hall.

world.name: White Rabbit's house
world.summary: The neat little house belonging to the White Rabbit, where Alice grows too large to leave.
world.body: A neat little house belonging to the White Rabbit, with a tidy room containing a table, looking-glass, and a bright brass plate on the door engraved 'W. RABBIT'. There is a little house about four feet high in an open place near where Alice ends the chapter.

world.name: Beautiful Garden
world.summary: The lovely garden Alice sees through the little door and enters in Ch 7

world.name: Wood
world.summary: A forest area containing the Tree in the wood, Mushroom, and houses

world.name: golden key
world.summary: A tiny key found on the glass table that fits the lock of the little door.
world.body: A tiny golden key found on the glass table that fits the lock of the little door.

events.what: Left on the three-legged table when Alice shrank and could no longer reach it.

world.name: DRINK ME bottle
world.summary: A little bottle whose contents cause the drinker to shrink.
world.body: A little bottle with a paper label reading 'DRINK ME' that appeared on the glass table and whose contents cause the drinker to shrink.

world.name: EAT ME cake
world.summary: A very small cake that causes the eater to grow.
world.body: A very small cake found in a glass box under the table, with the words 'EAT ME' marked in currants.

world.name: Hatter's watch
world.summary: A funny watch that tells the day of the month but not the time of day, damaged by butter and crumbs.
world.body: A funny watch that tells the day of the month but not the time of day, damaged by butter and crumbs.

world.name: Hookah
world.summary: A smoking pipe used by the Caterpillar while sitting on the mushroom.

world.name: Little cakes
world.summary: Small cakes transformed from pebbles thrown into the Rabbit's house, which cause the eater to shrink.
world.body: Pebbles thrown into the Rabbit's house turn into little cakes upon hitting the floor, which cause the eater to shrink.

events.what: Pebbles thrown into the White Rabbit's house turned into little cakes upon hitting the floor.

world.name: Mushroom
world.summary: A perfectly round mushroom whose two sides have opposite effects on the size of whoever eats them.
world.body: One side of the mushroom makes the eater grow taller, and the other side makes them grow shorter.

world.name: the verses
world.summary: An unsigned, undirected set of verses picked up and read as evidence at the Knave's trial.
world.body: An unsigned, undirected set of verses picked up and read as evidence at the Knave's trial.

world.name: three-legged table
world.summary: A solid glass table standing in the middle of the Hall of Doors, holding the golden key and the DRINK ME bottle.
world.body: A little table made entirely of solid glass, standing in the middle of the hall.

world.name: White Rabbit's fan
world.summary: A fan carried by the White Rabbit that causes Alice to shrink rapidly when she holds it.
world.body: The White Rabbit's fan causes Alice to shrink rapidly when she holds it.

events.what: Dropped by Alice when she shrank rapidly after using it.

world.name: Caucus-race
world.summary: A race with no set start or finish used to get dry.
world.body: A Caucus-race involves running in a rough circle with no set start or stop until everyone is dry, at which point everyone wins.

world.name: Lobster Quadrille
world.summary: A sea-shore dance involving lines of sea creatures advancing, changing lobster partners, and throwing them out to sea.
world.body: The dance involves forming two lines along the sea-shore, advancing twice with lobster partners, changing partners, and throwing the lobsters out to sea.

world.name: Rule Forty-two
world.summary: A rule in the King's note-book stating that all persons more than a mile high must leave the court.
world.body: A rule in the King's note-book stating that all persons more than a mile high must leave the court.

world.name: Time
world.summary: Personified as a 'him' who can be spoken to and who controls the clocks.
world.body: Time is personified as a 'him' who can be spoken to and who controls the clocks.

world.name: Wonderland
world.summary: The dream-world Alice falls into, where size is unstable, animals speak, and logic follows its own rules.
world.body: All of Alice's adventures in Wonderland were a dream. It is accessed by falling down the rabbit-hole and contains underground halls, woods, houses, a sea-shore, and a court of justice populated by talking animals and living playing cards.
